issues.t: Crank or cam sensor can make the engine stall (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light, hard starting, or the engine cutting out while driving.
issues.why: Solder joints on the circuit board inside the crankshaft and camshaft position sensors can crack from heat, so the engine computer loses its timing signal.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Ask an Infiniti dealer to check your VIN; the recall replaced these sensors free.

issues.t: Loss of power or stalling from a failing crank sensor
issues.sym: The engine hesitates, loses power, stalls at various speeds, or won't restart until it cools down. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The crankshaft position (angle) sensor can fail with age, even on cars that already had the recall work, and the engine computer can't run the engine without its signal.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Treat stalling as a safety problem. Have the codes read; a sensor replacement is usually the fix.

issues.t: Seat side airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may flash or stay on, but often there is no sign at all.
issues.why: A wiring connector under the front seats for the side airbags can build up electrical resistance, which can stop the side airbags from deploying in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer modifies the connector free. Get any airbag light checked promptly.

issues.t: Alternator can short and overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic or electrical smell, smoke from the engine bay, a battery light, or a dead battery.
issues.why: A diode in the alternator could be damaged when it was made. It can fail and short, melting the alternator housing, and the fumes could catch fire.
issues.next: If you smell burning plastic or see smoke, pull over and turn the engine off. Check the VIN; the alternator replacement under the recall is free.

issues.t: Key comes out without the shifter in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can turn the car off and remove the key while the shifter is not in Park.
issues.why: The shift lock control unit didn't work as required. If the car is left out of Park without the parking brake, it can roll away.
issues.next: Always put it in Park and set the parking brake. Check the VIN; dealers replace the shift lock control unit free.

issues.t: 17-inch alloy wheels can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration, a wobble, or a tire that keeps losing air. Cracks may be visible on the wheel.
issues.why: Some 17-inch wheels had a casting flaw that lets cracks grow while driving. A wheel could break and come off the hub.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the wheels inspected. Don't drive on a wheel with a visible crack.

issues.t: Brake lights may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: Your brake lights don't light when you press the brake pedal.
issues.why: The brake lamp switch could malfunction, so drivers behind you get no warning that you are stopping.
issues.next: Have someone check the brake lights. Check the VIN; dealers replace the switch free.

issues.t: Tail lamps don't meet brake light rules (recall)
issues.sym: You may not notice anything; the brake and reflector parts of the tail lamps are not as visible as required.
issues.why: The rear combination lamps did not meet federal standards for stop lamps and reflectors.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers replace the rear lamp assemblies free.

issues.t: Jerky shifts or slipping automatic transmission
issues.sym: Hard shifts from first to second, jerking, vibration when shifting, or the engine revving without the car speeding up.
issues.why: Owners report harsh shifting and slipping on these cars as the transmission ages. Skipped fluid changes make it worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Have the transmission scanned for codes before it slips badly; a service or valve body repair may avoid a rebuild.

issues.t: Check engine light from EVAP purge valve
issues.sym: Check engine light with no change in how the car drives. You may notice a slight fuel smell.
issues.why: The purge control valve in the evaporative emissions system fails, so fuel vapor isn't handled as the computer expects.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel cap is tight. If the light stays on, have the codes read; a purge valve is a simple fix.

issues.t: Knock sensor fault causes surging or poor power
issues.sym: Surging or uneven idle, sluggish acceleration, and a knock sensor trouble code.
issues.why: The knock sensor sits under the intake manifold and fails with age or heat, so the computer pulls back timing to protect the engine.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed. Replacement means removing the intake, so shops often replace the wiring at the same time.

issues.t: Cracked intake air duct causes rough running
issues.sym: Rough or unstable idle, hesitation, or a check engine light for a lean condition.
issues.why: The rubber air tube insulator around the throttle body cracks with age and lets in air the engine computer can't measure.
issues.next: Inspect the rubber intake parts for cracks and replace any cracked one.

issues.t: Cracked plastic engine cooling fan
issues.sym: A rattle or flutter from the front of the engine, or visible cracks in the fan blades or hub.
issues.why: The plastic engine-driven fan cracks with heat and age. A fan that breaks apart can damage the radiator.
issues.next: Inspect the fan when the engine is off. Replace it with a new fan if any cracks appear.

issues.t: Broken front coil spring
issues.sym: A loud clunk, the car sitting lower at one corner, or a tire being cut by a broken spring.
issues.why: Front coil springs can corrode and snap. An owner reported a broken front spring that punctured the tire and led to a loss of steering.
issues.next: If one corner sits low or you hear a bang, stop and inspect the spring. Don't drive on a broken spring.

issues.t: Worn front struts knocking
issues.sym: Knocking or tapping from the front over bumps, or a bouncy ride.
issues.why: Struts and bushings wear out with age. Owners commonly replace shocks and struts around 80,000 to 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the struts and mounts checked. Replace them in pairs.

issues.t: Power tilt or telescoping steering column stops working
issues.sym: The steering wheel won't move in or out, or gets stuck in the raised position.
issues.why: The motor or switch for the power steering column fails with age.
issues.next: If the wheel is stuck in a position you can't steer comfortably from, don't drive it. Have the switch and motor tested.

issues.t: Worn shocks or sport mode stops working
issues.sym: A floaty or bouncy ride, or the Sport suspension setting has no effect.
issues.why: These cars use electronically adjustable shocks. The shocks wear out around 100,000 miles, and owners report the sport mode failing after shock work.
issues.next: Have the shocks and their wiring checked; use parts that support the adjustable damping.

issues.t: Dash display goes dark
issues.sym: The center screen goes dark, or the navigation and climate display stop working.
issues.why: The fluorescent backlight in the display fails with age. Owners also report the screen joystick failing.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Specialist repair services can rebuild the display for less than a new unit.

issues.t: Headlight HID bulbs burn out
issues.sym: One low beam goes out, flickers or changes color.
issues.why: The xenon (HID) low beams wear out, and frequent on-off switching from the automatic headlights can shorten their life. Changing them means removing body parts.
issues.next: Replace the bulb soon; driving with one low beam is unsafe and can get you a ticket.

issues.t: Rear window sunshade stuck
issues.sym: The power rear window sunshade won't go up or down.
issues.why: Small plastic tabs in the sunshade mechanism break. Infiniti issued service document ITB01-065a covering the repair.
issues.next: Have the tabs replaced; this is not a safety issue.

issues.t: Power seat motor burns out
issues.sym: A power seat stops moving in one direction, or you smell burning electronics near the seat.
issues.why: A power seat motor can burn out. One owner reported this on a 2004 at about 66,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the seat switch and motor tested.

issues.t: Airbag warning light stays on
issues.sym: The supplemental airbag warning shows on the screen or the light stays on.
issues.why: Owners report airbag lights after low battery voltage or a power loss, and from faults in the side airbag wiring.
issues.next: Airbags may not work while the light is on. Have the codes read, and check the VIN for the side airbag recall.

issues.t: No crank from failing starter relays
issues.sym: You turn the key and nothing happens, or the car only starts after the battery is disconnected for a while.
issues.why: On this generation the two starter relays on the passenger-side firewall wear out; owners replaced starters before finding the relays.
issues.next: Have a shop test the relays before replacing the starter.

issues.t: Car pulls from low rear-steer (HICAS) fluid
issues.sym: The car pulls to one side, worse in turns. Only cars with rear-wheel steering (Q45t) are affected.
issues.why: The rear steering system has its own fluid reservoir. When it runs low, the rear wheels can stick off-center.
issues.next: Check the separate HICAS reservoir and look for leaks. Have alignment checked after topping up.

issues.t: Idler pulley seizes and belt snaps
issues.sym: A squeal or grinding from the front of the engine, then the belt snaps; the battery light comes on and steering gets heavy.
issues.why: A worn idler pulley bearing stops spinning freely and destroys the drive belt.
issues.next: If the belt snaps, stop driving; the alternator and power steering no longer work. Replace the pulley and belt together.
